summary: LLM inference costs scale linearly with token usage, and most production workloads waste 50-80% of their spend through uncached repeated prompts, oversized models, and verbose outputs. Stacking five to six optimization levers—prompt caching, semantic caching, model routing, output constraints, batching, and quantization—reliably achieves 70-85% total cost reduction without measurable quality loss. A real-world reputation SaaS cut its bill 79% (from $41.60 to $8.90 per 1,000 replies) using exactly this stacked approach.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching
techniques.description: Reuse previously processed input tokens (system prompts, large context, few-shot examples) server-side so repeated requests don't reprocess them. Providers charge a fraction for cache hits on identical prefixes.
techniques.savings: 41-80% on API costs, up to 90% on cached input tokens
techniques.example: On Anthropic, mark your 10,000-token system prompt with cache_control; subsequent calls within the TTL pay only 10% for those cached tokens. Anthropic requires prompts >1,024 tokens (Haiku) or >2,048 tokens (Sonnet/Opus) to be cacheable.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Cache responses keyed by embedding similarity rather than exact match, so semantically equivalent queries ('how do I reset my password' vs 'password reset help') return a stored answer without an LLM call.
techniques.savings: up to 73% cost reduction; 45% typical cache hit rate
techniques.example: Use GPTCache or Redis semantic cache to embed incoming queries; if cosine similarity to a cached query exceeds 0.95, serve the stored response and skip the API call entirely.

techniques.name: Model Routing
techniques.description: Route each request to the cheapest model capable of handling it—classification and extraction to budget tiers, complex reasoning to flagship models—instead of sending everything to the most expensive model.
techniques.example: Send 70% of traffic to GPT-3.5/Gemini Flash, 25% to GPT-4o-mini/Haiku, and only 5% to GPT-4/Opus based on task complexity; routing alone saved $24.50 per 1,000 calls in one documented case.

techniques.name: Output Constraints
techniques.description: Cap and structure output since output tokens cost 4-5x input tokens. Set low max_tokens, use structured output schemas (JSON mode), and instruct the model to be concise.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and request a JSON schema instead of a prose explanation, preventing runaway multi-paragraph responses on a model charging $10-15 per million output tokens.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Trim system prompts, remove filler phrases, replace multiple few-shot examples with one clear example, and compress context to reduce input token count on every call.
techniques.example: Cut a verbose 600-token system prompt to under 200 tokens by removing redundant instructions; a 30% reduction in prompt length translates directly to a 30% input-cost reduction across all calls.

techniques.name: Batch Processing
techniques.description: Submit non-urgent requests through provider batch APIs that process asynchronously (within 24h) for roughly half the per-token price.
techniques.savings: 50% off batched requests; up to 95% when combined with caching
techniques.example: Route nightly bulk tasks like review summarization through Anthropic's Batch API (50% off) combined with prompt caching (90% off cached tokens) to approach 95% savings.

techniques.name: Right-Sizing & Model Selection
techniques.description: Pick the smallest model tier that meets quality requirements and match GPU provisioning to actual usage for self-hosted inference, avoiding paying flagship rates for simple tasks.
techniques.example: A support chatbot at 1M conversations/month costs $3,250 on a flagship $2.50/$10 model; switching appropriate traffic to a budget tier cuts that several-fold with no quality drop on routine queries.

techniques.name: Quantization (Self-Hosted)
techniques.description: Reduce model weight precision (e.g. FP16 to INT8/INT4) to shrink memory footprint and increase throughput on open-source models you host yourself.
techniques.example: Serve a quantized INT4 Llama or Mistral model via vLLM to fit on a smaller GPU and double throughput versus the FP16 version.

techniques.name: Continuous Batching & KV Cache Reuse (Self-Hosted)
techniques.description: At the runtime layer, use continuous batching, PagedAttention, speculative decoding, and KV cache reuse to maximize GPU throughput instead of waiting for static batches.
techniques.example: Deploy vLLM or TGI with continuous batching so new requests join in-flight batches, raising a single H100's effective throughput 40-80% versus naive serving.

techniques.name: GPU Utilization Right-Sizing (Self-Hosted)
techniques.description: Avoid the #1 cost driver—under-utilized GPUs billed at 100% while running at 8-10% load. Match resource requests to real peak usage and autoscale.
techniques.savings: Large; eliminates up to ~90% idle waste
techniques.example: Teams often request an H100 80GB for a 9GB workload running at 8% utilization; right-sizing to a smaller instance or bin-packing with Cast AI eliminates the idle spend.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library that stores LLM responses and serves them for semantically similar queries via embedding similarity, cutting duplicate API calls.
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open-source (self-hosted; you pay only for any embedding/vector store infra)

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK for 100+ LLM providers offering model routing, fallbacks, load balancing, caching, and cost tracking through an OpenAI-compatible interface.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; Enterprise tier with SSO/support (custom pricing)

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing request logging, cost analytics, caching, and prompt management via a one-line proxy integration.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); paid plans from ~$20/month, plus enterprise

tools.name: Redis / Redis Semantic Cache
tools.description: In-memory data store with vector search used for exact-match and semantic LLM response caching plus session/context management in multi-tier caching strategies.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; Redis Cloud managed from ~$5/month and up

tools.name: LangChain
tools.description: LLM application framework with built-in caching integrations (in-memory, Redis, SQLite, semantic), prompt templating, and routing for orchestrating cost-aware pipelines.
tools.pricing_paid: Open-source free; LangSmith observability paid plans from ~$39/user/month

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: High-throughput open-source inference engine implementing PagedAttention, continuous batching, and KV cache reuse for self-hosted model serving.
tools.pricing_paid: Free and open-source (you pay only for your own GPU infrastructure)

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API marketplace routing requests across many providers/models with automatic price comparison and fallbacks, enabling easy model routing.
tools.pricing_paid: Pay-as-you-go passthrough pricing with a small routing fee; no subscription required

tools.name: Cast AI
tools.description: Kubernetes cost optimization platform that right-sizes and bin-packs GPU workloads to eliminate idle capacity in self-hosted LLM inference fleets.
tools.pricing_paid: Free analysis tier; paid automation priced as a percentage of realized savings

quick_wins: Enable prompt caching on your long/static system prompts — a near-free config change that cuts input costs 41-80% on repeated calls.
Cut system prompts to under 200 tokens and remove filler phrases/redundant few-shot examples for an immediate ~30% input-token reduction.
Set a sensible max_tokens cap and switch to structured JSON output to halve expensive output tokens (which cost 4-5x input).
Route simple tasks (classification, extraction) to a budget model tier instead of sending everything to a flagship model, saving 40-70%.
Add an exact-match plus semantic response cache (Redis or GPTCache) to avoid paying for repeated or near-identical queries, targeting a ~45% hit rate.
